policy: Classify the abstract mathematical content separately from P000 interpretation. NO_MATERIAL_MATCH is not novelty; absence from exact-phrase searches is never enough by itself. Published monographs/papers and standard project references are preferred over recent secondary discussions.

sources.citation: Wilfrid Hodges, Model Theory, Cambridge University Press, 1993, Chapter 4: Automorphisms.
sources.verified: Publisher chapter record inspected. Used only for the standard automorphism/definability framework.
sources.load_bearing: Definable/canonical structure must respect automorphisms of the underlying structure.

sources.citation: Leonard Tomczak, Model Theory – Lecture Notes, University of California, Berkeley, 2023, Proposition 7.5.
sources.verified: Accessible university-hosted notes state that a is in dcl(A) iff its orbit under Aut(U/A) is a singleton (in the stated monster-model setting), and explicitly prove definability implies automorphism invariance.
sources.load_bearing: Exact necessary implication used by Gen9: a moved candidate cannot be definable/canonical over the fixed parameters.

sources.citation: Christopher Godsil and Karen Meagher, Erdős–Ko–Rado Theorems: Algebraic Approaches, Cambridge University Press, 2015, Chapter 14: Permutations.
sources.verified: Publisher text inspected; it states that the pointwise stabilizer of t distinct elements in Sym(n) has size (n-t)!.
sources.load_bearing: The exact S6 residual-stabilizer sequence after k anchors.

sources.citation: Robert F. Bailey and Peter J. Cameron, Base sizes, metric dimension and other invariants of groups and graphs, survey/preprint.
sources.verified: University-hosted preprint inspected; Definition 2.1 defines a base as a subset with trivial pointwise stabilizer.
sources.load_bearing: Classical permutation-group base terminology; for natural S6 the preceding stabilizer formula gives base size 5.

sources.citation: The Stacks Project, Section 39.11: Principal homogeneous spaces, Lemma 39.11.2 and Definition 39.11.3.
sources.verified: Current Stacks text inspected; pseudo G-torsor is characterized by a simply transitive G-action on T-points, and triviality is equivalent to a section.
sources.load_bearing: Standard torsor/principal-homogeneous-space semantics used to identify the set of frames as an S6-torsor.

sources.citation: Ralph L. Cohen, The Topology of Fiber Bundles / Math 215B notes, Stanford University.
sources.verified: University-hosted notes inspected. Theorem 2.4 states a principal G-bundle is trivial iff it has a section; Definition 4.5 defines the gauge group as bundle automorphisms lying over the identity of the base.
sources.load_bearing: A frame/section as trivialization and the fact that gauge changes are vertical presentation changes fixing base points.

sources.citation: Tingran Gao, Jacek Brodzki, Sayan Mukherjee, The Geometry of Synchronization Problems and Learning Group Actions, Discrete & Computational Geometry 65(1) (2021), 150–211.
sources.verified: Published article metadata and accepted-manuscript abstract inspected. It identifies synchronization on a connected graph with flat principal G-bundles and states that triviality of holonomy dictates synchronizability.
sources.load_bearing: Graph edge transports, synchronization, principal-bundle interpretation, holonomy obstruction, and the crucial distinction between flat-bundle language and trivial holonomy needed for a global synchronized frame.

sources.citation: Ruy Exel, Partial actions of groups and actions of inverse semigroups, Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society 126(12) (1998), 3481–3494.
sources.verified: Author/arXiv abstract and bibliographic metadata inspected; it states a one-to-one correspondence between partial actions of a group and actions of the canonical inverse semigroup S(G).
sources.load_bearing: Standard abstract mechanism for domain-sensitive partial actions; partiality is existing mathematics, not a P000-specific invention.

sources.citation: W. D. Munn, The characters of the symmetric inverse semigroup, Mathematical Proceedings of the Cambridge Philosophical Society 53(1) (1957), 13–18.
sources.verified: Publisher extract inspected; it describes the symmetric inverse semigroup as the partial transformations/partial one-to-one maps analogue of the symmetric group.
sources.load_bearing: Partial bijections as a classical algebraic object.

sources.citation: MIT 18.700 Linear Algebra, Day 10 lecture plan, Proposition 19 (Change of basis formula).
sources.verified: MIT-hosted notes inspected; Proposition 19 gives the standard conjugation/similarity change-of-basis formula.
sources.load_bearing: PASS as ordinary frame reindexing; conjugation is appropriate only if M is an operator matrix.

sources.citation: Katrin Tent and Martin Ziegler, A Course in Model Theory, Cambridge University Press, 2012, §1.2 Many-sorted structures.
sources.verified: Publisher excerpt inspected; many-sorted languages carry typed function and relation symbols with specified domain/range sorts.
sources.load_bearing: The mere use of Cell/axis/channel sorts and typed cross-sort relations is standard; what remains project-specific is the exact P000 ontology and no-quotient rule.

negative_search_boundary: Exact-phrase and concept searches did not locate an external mathematical source defining the exact compound P000 rule: opaque native Cell identity + native-axis sort + local PF-10 channel presentation + carrier/readout nonidentity + explicit no-quotient semantics.

Searches for AXIS_CHANNEL_FRAME outside the project did not produce a material mathematical duplicate; hits for 'cell identity' were dominated by unrelated telecommunications/biology uses and were excluded.

Standard gauge theory already fixes base points under vertical gauge transformations, and many-sorted logic already supplies typed relations; these partial overlaps prevent any claim that the ingredients themselves are novel.
The negative result is NO_MATERIAL_MATCH for the exact compound package only. It does not establish novelty, inventive step, patentability, or publication originality.
terminology_finding: The strongest correction from the audit is terminological: standard flatness permits nontrivial global holonomy/monodromy. The condition equivalent to a globally parallel frame field is trivial holonomy (synchronizability/pure gauge), not flatness alone.
